paper_title: Quantum Walks on Simplicial Complexes and Harmonic Homology: Application to Topological Data Analysis with Superpolynomial Speedups
authors: Ryu Hayakawa; Kuo-Chin Chen; Min-Hsiu Hsieh

For non-constant k, this best known classical direct-solver approach takes superpolynomial time. Hence, the quantum algorithm of Theorem 7 indicates an apparent superpolynomial speedup over the best known classical algorithm whenever λmin = Ω(1/poly(n)). We leave showing a quantum speedup for HDDP under plausible computational complexity assumptions as an open problem. We remark that the assumption ∥Qf ∥ = Ω(∥f ∥) is natural, since it holds whenever the boundary cochain f is not concentrated on simplices that are decoupled from the interior. When ∥Qf ∥ is exponentially small, the preparation of |r⟩ requires exponentially many repetitions, and the complexity of the HDDP in this regime remains an open problem.
